Cleaning¶

First we convert the observation date to datetime.

In [ ]:
df['observation_date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['observation_date'])

Then we create a new data table with the inflation rate of each category (percent change) and add the total inflation to a new column in the original data frame, this will be the dependent variable. Lastly, we have to remove the first row as percent change cant be calculated from the first entry.

In [ ]:
inflation_df = df.copy()
inflation_df.iloc[:, 1:] = df.iloc[:, 1:].pct_change() * 100

df['Total_Inflation'] = inflation_df.iloc[:, 1:].mean(axis=1)
df = df.drop(index=0).reset_index(drop=True)
df[['observation_date', 'Total_Inflation']].head()

The Mean Squared Error quantifies the average squared difference between the actual and predicted CPI values.

Decision tree classification and Evaluation.¶

In [ ]:
# Feature selection

features = [
    'MedicalInsurance', 'Recreation', 'Food&Beverages',
    'Tuition&ChildCare', 'Airfare', 'HouseRent',
    'Electricity', 'Auto_Fuel', 'Cable&Communication'
]

X = df[features]
y = df['Inflation_Level']

# Scale the features
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)
In [ ]:
# Split dataset

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X_scaled, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42, stratify=y
)
# Decision Tree Classifier

dt_model = DecisionTreeClassifier(
    criterion='entropy', max_depth=4, random_state=42
)
dt_model.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Evaluation

y_pred = dt_model.predict(X_test)

print("\nClassification Report:\n", classification_report(y_test, y_pred))
print("Accuracy Score:", accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred))

Evaluation Metrics - F1 Score and Recall

The F1-score balances both false positives and false negatives Recall measures how many of the actual “positive” (or high inflation) cases were correctly identified.

In [ ]:
from sklearn.metrics import f1_score, recall_score

# Compute metrics
f1 = f1_score(y_test, y_pred, average='weighted')
recall = recall_score(y_test, y_pred, average='weighted')

# Create data for plotting
metrics = ['F1-Score', 'Recall']
values = [f1, recall]

# Scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(6,4))
plt.scatter(metrics, values, color='blue', s=100)

# Annotate points
for i, val in enumerate(values):
    plt.text(metrics[i], val + 0.01, f"{val:.3f}", ha='center', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')

# Labels and title

plt.title("Decision Tree Performance Metrics (F1-Score vs Recall)")
plt.xlabel("Metric")
plt.ylabel("Score")
plt.ylim(0, 1.05)
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
plt.show()

Time Series Analysis

Use Exponential Smoothing to forecast future CPI trends and detect seasonality.

Import packages

In [ ]:
from statsmodels.tsa.holtwinters import ExponentialSmoothing

Prepare the data for processing

In [ ]:
# Convert observation_date to datetime and set as index

df['observation_date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['observation_date'])
df = df.sort_values(by='observation_date')
df.set_index('observation_date', inplace=True)

# House Rent is the representative component
ts = df['HouseRent']

# Apply Exponential Smoothing Model

# Fit model with trend and seasonality detection
model = ExponentialSmoothing(
    ts,
    trend='add',             # captures upward/downward trend
    seasonal='add',          # additive seasonality
    seasonal_periods=12      # adjust based on monthly data
).fit()

/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/statsmodels/tsa/base/tsa_model.py:473: ValueWarning: No frequency information was provided, so inferred frequency MS will be used.
  self._init_dates(dates, freq)

Forecast future values and plot Actual vs Forecast

In [ ]:
# Forecast future values

forecast_periods = 12  # forecast 12 months ahead
forecast = model.forecast(steps=forecast_periods)

# Plot actual vs forecast

plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
plt.plot(ts, label='Actual CPI - House Rent', linewidth=2)
plt.plot(forecast, label='Forecasted CPI', linestyle='--', color='red')
plt.title("CPI Forecast (House Rent) using Exponential Smoothing")
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("CPI Index")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
plt.show()

Plot fitted values vs Actual values

In [ ]:
# Step 6: Plot fitted values vs actual
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
plt.plot(ts, label='Actual Data', linewidth=2)
plt.plot(model.fittedvalues, label='Fitted Values', linestyle='--', color='orange')
plt.title("Fitted vs Actual CPI (House Rent) - Exponential Smoothing")
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("CPI Index")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
plt.show()

Evaluation Metrics - MSE and RMSE

  1. Mean Squared Error (MSE) quantifies the average squared difference between the actual and predicted (fitted) CPI values.

  2. Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) RMSE is the square root of MSE, bringing the error value back to the same unit as the CPI index

In [ ]:
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error

Compute MSE and RMSE and plot the scatter graphs

In [ ]:
# Compute evaluation metrics using fitted values
mse = mean_squared_error(ts, model.fittedvalues)
rmse = np.sqrt(mse)

print(f"Mean Squared Error (MSE): {mse:.3f}")
print(f"Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE): {rmse:.3f}")

# Plot scatter for visual comparison
metrics = ['MSE', 'RMSE']
values = [mse, rmse]

plt.figure(figsize=(6,4))
plt.scatter(metrics, values, color='green', s=100)

for i, val in enumerate(values):
    plt.text(metrics[i], val + 0.01, f"{val:.3f}", ha='center', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')

plt.title("Forecast Evaluation Metrics - Exponential Smoothing")
plt.xlabel("Metric")
plt.ylabel("Error Value")
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
plt.show()

Mean Squared Error (MSE): 0.059
Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE): 0.242
